S025.name: Loss_of_Interest
S025.description: A state where interest or pleasure in previously enjoyed activities is markedly diminished.

subtypes.Loss of Interest: Reduced interest in previously enjoyed hobbies or leisure activities.
subtypes.Social Withdrawal: Reduced interest or effort in social interactions and maintaining relationships.
subtypes.Loss of Motivation: Lack of motivation to initiate or complete work or tasks.
subtypes.Anhedonia: Inability to experience positive emotions such as happiness, satisfaction, love, or pleasure.
subtypes.Indifference to Achievement: Insensitivity or indifference to personal achievements or success.

S026.name: Weight_Appetite_Change
S026.description: Significant increase or decrease in appetite or weight.

subtypes.Significant Weight Loss: Weight loss of more than 5% in a month without dieting.
subtypes.Weight Gain: Weight gain of more than 5% in a month.
subtypes.Decrease in Appetite: Decrease in appetite occurring nearly every day.
subtypes.Increase in Appetite: Increase in appetite occurring nearly every day.

S027.name: Sleep_Disturbance
S027.description: A state where there is a significant change in the quantity or quality of sleep.

subtypes.Initial Insomnia: Difficulty falling asleep and taking a long time to do so.
subtypes.Middle Insomnia: Waking up frequently during sleep or having difficulty falling back asleep.
subtypes.Early Morning Awakening: Waking up too early and being unable to fall back asleep.
subtypes.Hypersomnia: Sleeping for long periods at night or excessive sleep during the day.
subtypes.Nightmare Disorder: Sleep disturbance caused by repeated and distressing dreams.
subtypes.Non-Restorative Sleep: Feeling unrefreshed despite having slept enough.

S029.name: Fatigue
S029.description: Persistent fatigue that is not relieved by rest and a marked lack of energy.

subtypes.Chronic Fatigue: Fatigue that persists for a long period even after adequate rest.
subtypes.Physical Fatigue: A state of physical exhaustion where the body feels heavy and easily tires even from minor activities.
subtypes.Mental Fatigue: A state where fatigue accumulates rapidly during the process of thinking or concentrating.
subtypes.Loss of Energy: Difficulty performing daily activities due to a decline in energy and vitality.

S030.name: Worthlessness_Guilt
S030.description: Feelings of worthlessness or excessive or inappropriate guilt (which may be delusional; not merely self-reproach or guilt about being sick).

subtypes.Feelings of Worthlessness: The feeling that one is useless and has no value.
subtypes.Ruminative Guilt: A thought pattern of obsessively replaying past minor mistakes or flaws and constantly reproaching oneself.
subtypes.Excessive or Inappropriate Guilt: Feeling excessive responsibility for trivial matters or daily events and believing one deserves punishment.
subtypes.Delusional Guilt: Guilt reaching a delusional level, disconnected from reality, involving feeling responsible for unrelated unfortunate events.

S031.name: Diminished_Thinking
S031.description: Diminished ability to think or concentrate, or indecisiveness.

subtypes.Reduced Concentration: Unable to pay attention or maintain focus on specific activities like conversation, reading, or watching TV.
subtypes.Indecisiveness: Extreme difficulty making even minor daily choices (e.g., menu, clothes) and hesitating to make decisions.
subtypes.Subjective Memory Complaints: Complaining of memory decline, such as forgetting where things were placed, due to reduced focus.
subtypes.Clouded Thinking: Thinking feels foggy, dazed, or not clear.

S032.name: Death_Suicide
S032.description: Recurrent thoughts of death, recurrent suicidal ideation, or a suicide attempt.

subtypes.Recurrent Thoughts of Death: Passive wish to die (e.g., 'I wish I wouldn't wake up') without active intent to kill oneself.
subtypes.Suicidal Ideation: Recurring thoughts of 'I want to die' or 'I want to kill myself' without a specific plan.
subtypes.Suicidal Impulse: Strong, sudden urges to jump from a height or run into traffic without a concrete plan.
subtypes.Specific Plan for Suicide: Conceiving specific scenarios or methods regarding when, where, and how to die.
subtypes.Suicide Attempt: Actual actions taken to end one's life or preparatory behaviors like hoarding pills or writing a will.

symptom.disease_info: Major Depressive Disorder (MDD) is characterized by one or more episodes of at least two weeks of pervasive low mood or loss of interest, accompanied by cognitive and physical changes such as altered sleep or appetite, low energy, impaired concentration, and feelings of worthlessness or excessive guilt, leading to significant functional impairment. The clinical course can be single-episode or recurrent, with episodes often triggered or exacerbated by psychosocial stressors, medical illness, or substance use, though they may also arise without clear precipitants. Diagnosis requires that symptoms represent a change from prior functioning and are not better explained by bereavement alone, bipolar disorder, psychotic disorders, or the physiological effects of a substance or medical condition. Compared to adjustment disorders or normal sadness, MDD is more persistent, more impairing, and involves a broader constellation of affective, cognitive, and somatic symptoms, sometimes including thoughts of death or suicide.

patient.personality: A warm, community-oriented art lover who is conscientious and collaborative but prone to chronic worrying and self-criticism, finding solace in creative projects and small social gatherings.
patient.stressor: Catherine recently stepped back from her part-time library job and paused her coursework after relocating with her spouse to a new city for his career, abruptly losing the campus community and volunteer network that had anchored her days. Eager to re-create that sense of purpose, she threw herself into planning small art meetups and applying for community arts coordinator roles, but weeks of unanswered applications and logistical hurdles left her feeling as though she was failing both her own aspirations and the expectations she imagined others had for her. Without the familiar feedback and appreciation from classmates, patrons, and fellow volunteers, her long-standing tendency to worry turned inward, and she began to dwell on past perceived missteps, interpreting ordinary setbacks as proof that she was unreliable and undeserving of opportunities. Over the past month, these self-blaming thoughts intensified to the point that she began avoiding even low-stakes social gatherings and confided to her spouse that she felt like “dead weight,” leading them to encourage her to see a psychiatrist.
patient.chief_complaint: “I can’t shake this feeling that I’m a burden and failing everyone around me.”

S025.name: Loss_of_Interest
S025.description: A state where interest or pleasure in previously enjoyed activities is markedly diminished.
S025.manifestation: I used to get so much joy out of sketching at the park or organizing little art nights, but lately I just stare at my supplies or the meetup page and feel nothing, so I end up scrolling on my phone and canceling plans instead of following through.

S026.name: Weight_Appetite_Change
S026.description: Significant increase or decrease in appetite or weight.
S026.manifestation: Most days I have to remind myself to eat because food just doesn’t sound appealing, and I’ll suddenly realize it’s late afternoon and all I’ve had is coffee and maybe a piece of toast my spouse pushed on me.

S027.name: Sleep_Disturbance
S027.description: A state where there is a significant change in the quantity or quality of sleep.
S027.manifestation: At night I lie in bed for over an hour with my mind looping through everything I’m supposedly messing up, and even when I finally fall asleep I keep waking up and never feel rested in the morning.

S029.name: Fatigue
S029.description: Persistent fatigue that is not relieved by rest and a marked lack of energy.
S029.manifestation: Even simple things like taking a shower or walking to the corner store feel like they require this huge amount of effort, and I end up sitting on the couch feeling drained even though I haven’t really done anything all day.

S030.name: Worthlessness_Guilt
S030.description: Feelings of worthlessness or excessive or inappropriate guilt (which may be delusional; not merely self-reproach or guilt about being sick).
S030.manifestation: I keep thinking that I’m just dead weight—like my husband moved us here for his big opportunity and all I’ve done is mope and fail at getting involved, and I replay every little mistake I’ve made at past jobs or classes as proof that people were wrong to believe in me.

S031.name: Diminished_Thinking
S031.description: Diminished ability to think or concentrate, or indecisiveness.
S031.manifestation: It’s like my brain is full of fog—reading a page of a book or even filling out a simple job application takes forever because I lose my train of thought, and I’ll agonize for ten minutes over tiny decisions like which cereal to buy.

S032.name: Death_Suicide
S032.description: Recurrent thoughts of death, recurrent suicidal ideation, or a suicide attempt.
S032.manifestation: Pretty often I catch myself thinking it wouldn’t really matter if I didn’t wake up tomorrow, and on the worst days I imagine just disappearing so my husband wouldn’t have to deal with me, even though I haven’t made any plans to actually hurt myself.
